newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Soquimich signs China lithium deal.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Soquimich signs China lithium deal.

text.p: Chile's Sociedad Quimica y Minera de Chile (Soquimich) has signed a three year contract to supply lithium carbonate from its Minsal mine to China's CNIEC Xinjiang Corp, said a top Minsal official.
Under the contract, Xinjiang will buy around 20 percent of Minsal's lithium carbonate production, said Felipe Anguita, general manager of Socidad Minera Salar de Atacama.
Minsal, which came on stream in December, will produce 18,000-20,000 tonnes a year of lithium carbonate when operating at full capacity in 1998, he said.
"Output will be lower this year. But the Chinese will buy the same percentage of our 1997 production," Anguita told Reuters by telephone.
He said Minsal, which lies on a dry salt lake in the northern Atacama Desert, expects to produce 9,000 tonnes of lithium carbonate this year.
Xinjiang will use the lithium for production in its own plants and will resale the mineral to other consumers in China.
Minsal has already cornered 30-35 percent of the world lithium market in the three months since the Chilean-produced mineral first reached consumers, he said.
World lithium prices have fallen to $1,800 a tonne from $3,500 at the start of the year as a result of the company's agressive sales push, he said.
Soquimich, Chile's largest fertilizer-maker, may in future expand its lithium carbonate production and is already studying making other lithium compounds, said Anguita.
"We have the capacity to expand production...at marginal costs," he said.
Minsal will become the world's second largest lithium producer after Cyprus Amax Minerals.

Largest consumers of lithium carbonate, a fine white powder, are the glass, ceramics and primary aluminium industries. It is also used, in much smaller quantities, in pharmaceuticals as a well-known treatment for manic depression.
